top_signal.title: CPA, 1 year into e-commerce, not making money and feeling a bit lost
top_signal.summary: Hi everyone,   CPA here, and I’ve been wanting to get out of accounting for a while. Unless you make it to CFO level, the pay really isn’t what people think, and running my own business has always been the dream.   About a year ago I started selling online. Sales have actually been pretty good, but the profit just isn’t there. International shipping keeps getting more expensive, especially this Q4. On top of that, a lot of products need extra work before they’re ready to ship, and dealing with customers can be exhausting. More than once, tracking showed “delivered” but the buyer said it never arrived. After a year of this and seeing all kinds of situations, I’m honestly just tired of it.   So now I’m trying to figure out what’s next. Small consumer goods don’t feel like the answer; the market is so crowded and it’s hard to compete.    I’ve been curious about chemical products, but honestly have no idea where to start.    Another idea is becoming a sourcing agent. A lot of businesses source from China, and I could help them find and compare factories, check quality, and work on commission. Not sure if that’s realistic though.   A little about me: I speak fluent Mandarin, I’m very detail-oriented, and my customers have left a lot of great reviews. The CPA background helps with costs and margins too.   If you’ve been in a similar spot, or have any product ideas or thoughts on the sourcing agent route, I’d really love to hear them. Feeling a bit lost right now, so any advice mean
